approvedExclusions.reason: A cancelled PiSharp update stages downloads and retains the prior valid package; pinned Pi removes that package while the download is in flight.
A SIGKILL-interrupted PiSharp update recovers the prior valid package; pinned Pi leaves the package removed.
When SIGINT terminates the configured manager, pinned Pi leaves the partially created package directory while PiSharp cancels the child and removes the incomplete install.
If dependency installation fails during a Git update, pinned Pi leaves the updated source checkout active while PiSharp keeps the prior valid checkout through staged replacement.
When a bulk npm update is cancelled during download, pinned Pi removes the package while PiSharp retains the previous valid version through staged replacement.
When settings.json cannot be replaced, pinned Pi exits successfully while leaving the installed package unconfigured; PiSharp reports the write failure and also leaves it unconfigured.
Pi leaves an empty npm package root after an interrupted initial install; PiSharp removes the incomplete staging root.
When settings.json cannot be replaced, pinned Pi exits successfully while leaving the installed package unconfigured; PiSharp reports the write failure and also leaves it unconfigured.
A SIGKILL-interrupted PiSharp npm update retains its staged last-good package while pinned Pi has removed the installed package.
After SIGKILL during npm update, pinned Pi cannot list the removed package on restart while PiSharp restarts successfully with version 1.0.0.
While npm update downloads a replacement, pinned Pi temporarily removes the usable package from discovery; PiSharp keeps version 1.0.0 discoverable until version 1.1.0 is published.

Pinned Pi runs concurrent npm installs against the same target; npm can remove the package directory while the other process reads it, returning ENOENT and leaving no configured package. PiSharp serializes the installs and publishes one valid package; the verifier accepts only this captured target-path race and a clean PiSharp state.

Pinned Pi can race while two processes clone the same Git package, report an invalid origin/HEAD ref and leave it unconfigured. PiSharp serializes the install and publishes one valid package; the verifier accepts only this captured upstream race and safe final PiSharp state.
